newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cesp sees Eurobond roadshow in April, May.
newsitem.headline: Cesp sees Eurobond roadshow in April, May.

text.p: Sao Paulo state electricity company Cesp plans to do a roadshow by late April or early May for its $200 million eight-year Eurobond, Cesp international director Octavio de Barros said.
"We will probably issue in May and do a roadshow at the end of April or the beginning of May," Barros said.

Barros had originally thought the bond, led by J.P. Morgan, would be issued in March. But the market turned sour last month ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve Board's 25 basis point rise in short-term interest rates, causing many issuers to postpone their deals.
The bond will be put-able at five years and will not have a guarantee from the federal government, Barros said.

Market sources said Parana state electricity company Copel would begin a roadshow for its $150 million eight- year deal, put-able at five, this week. Officials from Copel and lead manager Santander were not available for comment.
Federally owned power generator Furnas was expected to begin its roadshow for a $90 million Eurobond within two weeks.
